skills\gateway\SKILL.md:31:A node's `## Links` lines name related nodes as `[[slug]]`, with the relation in words. When the answer needs a second subject ("who employs the supervisor of X"), follow the link: find its row in `index.md`, then open it by path. A link to a slug with no index row means the brain has nothing on it.
rationale\decisions\D02-node-identity.md:50:- A link line is `- <relation> [[slug]]`, where the relation text is required.
requirements\scoping-phase-1b.md:16:| Structural pass | Built from written `[[links]]` and frontmatter: no model, free, identical every run, rerun on every file change | D7, D8 |
requirements\scoping-phase-1b.md:53:[Omitted long matching line]
requirements\scoping-phase-1b.md:67:- **Link reasons are lost.** Every `[[wikilink]]` becomes a bare `references` edge, so the reason text on each link (the plan's "labelled relationship") doesn't survive. Our `aliases` aren't used either, since resolution is by filename only.
requirements\scoping-phase-1b.md:73:   - **Our structural pass.** It reads every markdown file in the brain, takes the frontmatter and every hand-written `[[link]]`, and writes `graph.json`: no model, free, identical every run, re-run on every file change. It keeps what Graphify drops: each link's reason text and the frontmatter aliases (D31). It's ours, in the repo, not a fork of Graphify.
requirements\scoping-phase-1b.md:84:- **Alias resolution has no real-corpus coverage yet (2026-10-25).** Structural-pass criterion 4 is covered by unit tests only (`[[Mattingly]]` resolving to `ken-mattingly`). All 143 Apollo links resolved by slug, because none in that corpus are written as an alias. The Apollo brain is deliberately **not** edited to add alias links, since that would write the test's answer into the corpus. Real coverage comes when Manoj's own brain is in, since he writes links by alias.
requirements\spec-phase-1a.md:50:6. Given any link line, when it is parsed, then it has relation text and one `[[slug]]`.
requirements\spec-phase-1a.md:53:7a. Given a link `[[x]]` where `x` equals the normalized form of one of a node's aliases, when it is resolved through `index.md`, then it reaches that node. Given a name typed as written (for example `Bank Work`), when it is normalized, then it matches the same node.
requirements\spec-phase-1b-structural-pass.md:10:A model-free pass that reads every node in a brain and writes the map as `.map/graph.json`. It uses only what is written down: frontmatter and the hand-written `[[links]]`. It keeps what Graphify drops (each link's reason text, and alias resolution), it is deterministic, and it is rebuildable at any time (D6). Graphify's discovery pass is out of scope here; this spec covers only the map.

62	    """Lines (number, text) inside the `## Links` section, up to the next heading."""
63	    out, inside = [], False
64	    for offset, line in enumerate(body):

67	            continue
68	        if inside:

73	def parse_node(path: Path, root: Path) -> tuple[Node | None, str | None]:
74	    rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
75	    parts = _split(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
76	    if parts is None:
77	        return None, "no frontmatter block"
78	    fm_text, body, first_line = parts
79	    try:
80	        fm = yaml.safe_load(fm_text) or {}
81	    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
82	        return None, f"unparseable frontmatter: {exc.__class__.__name__}"
83	    missing = [k for k in ("id", "slug", "name", "type") if not fm.get(k)]
84	    if missing:
85	        return None, f"missing frontmatter field(s): {', '.join(missing)}"
86	    node = Node(
87	        id=str(fm["id"]),
88	        slug=str(fm["slug"]),
89	        name=str(fm["name"]),
90	        type=str(fm["type"]),
91	        path=rel,
92	        aliases=[str(a) for a in fm.get("aliases") or []],
93	    )
94	    for number, line in links_section(body, first_line):
95	        m = LINK_LINE.match(line)
96	        if m:
